citations.locator: Old-Catholic Mariavite Church in Poland, member profile
citations.excerpt: This community was founded in 1906 in Warsaw by a diocesan priest and a sister of the Third Order of Franciscans.

facts.value: Stresses veneration of the Eucharist and the Virgin Mary. Recognizes the first seven ecumenical councils but not papal primacy or infallibility.

citations.excerpt: They stressed the veneration of the eucharist and the blessed Virgin Mary.
The new church recognized the first seven ecumenical councils but rejected papal primacy and infallibility.

facts.value: A church received into the Old Catholics in 1909 that is no longer a member of the Union of Utrecht.

citations.excerpt: Negotiations with the members of the Utrecht Union culminated in the reception of the Mariavites into the Old-Catholics at their congress in Vienna in 1909.
Currently the church is not a member of the Old-Catholic Union of Utrecht.

facts.value_before_verify: A Polish church that grew from Franciscan-rule communities. It joined the Old Catholics in 1909 but is no longer a member of the Union of Utrecht.
